title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from the dossier title and notation). E is an ℓ-adic (or virtual) sheaf on a projective curve X over F_q, with E_η its generic fibre. Grothendieck's cohomological expression gives the global constant of the functional equation of L(X,E,t) as a determinant of Frobenius on cohomology. In the notes this determinant is written δ^q(E_η), and ε^q(E_η) is a normalised version of it.

For each closed point x there are local data:
- α_x(E_η), a local virtual representation (the local Galois/inertia data at x);
- μ_x(E), a local correction term, apparently built from α_x(E_η) and its dual, measuring the defect of duality at x;
- δ_x, a local determinant constant;
- χ_x(E_η), a local Euler characteristic or Swan/Artin-type exponent.

The page then argues as follows.
1. Poincaré duality and the 'formule virtuelle' for D(E_η^q), a duality or determinant identity, give δ^q(E)^{-1} = δ^q(E)·q^{-χ(E)(q+1)?}·∏_x δ_x(μ_x(E)). Global inversion is thus expressed through local terms.
2. A local computation gives δ(μ_x(E)) = δ_x(E_η)^{-2}·q^{χ_x(E_η)}.
3. Substituting gives ε^q(E_η)^2 = δ^q(E_η)^2/q^{χ^q(E)} = ∏_x δ_x(E_η)^2/q^{χ_x(E_η)}.
4. Taking square roots gives ε^q(E_η) = ±∏_x ε_x(E_η)·p^{-χ/2}, with ε_x = δ_x/q^{χ_x/2} and χ = Σ_x χ_x(E_η).

In modern terms this is the product formula for the global ε-constant as a product of local ε-constants, but only UP TO SIGN. The argument works by squaring, using self-duality / the functional equation, so that only ε^2 is determined. The full product formula was conjectured by Deligne (Antwerp II, 1973) and proved by Laumon (1987) via the ℓ-adic Fourier transform, i.e. local Fourier transforms and stationary phase. The page serves Grothendieck's project of an ℓ-adic theory of local constants in the geometric case.

The neighbouring pages (n° 392, a Bourbaki Algèbre commutative ch. VII draft on pseudo-null modules and reflexive lattices) are unrelated material filed in the same folder.
errors: The page mixes p and q in exponents. Examples are p^{-χ^q(E)(p+1)} in line 1, p^{-χ_x(E_η)(q+1)} inside the bracket, and p^{χ_x/2} and p^{χ/2} in the last lines. Since the final normalisation is by q^{χ/2}, the p's are almost certainly slips for q, or for the cardinality of the residue field at x. As written, the last displayed equality ε = (∏ δ_x/p^{χ_x/2})·p^{-χ/2} is not dimensionally consistent with the preceding line.

Signs of exponents are inconsistent between lines. Squaring δ^{-1} = δ·(…)·∏δ_x^{-2}q^{χ_x} gives ∏ δ_x^2/q^{χ_x} = δ^2·q^{(…)+Σχ_x}. That matches the 'd'où' line only if the global factor is chosen suitably. The line 'δ^2/q^{χ^q(E)} = q^{χ^q(E)}' is crossed out by Grothendieck himself.
The square-root step only yields the formula up to a sign ±. This sign is the genuine difficulty, later resolved by Laumon. The page does not address it.
A local degree factor is missing: q^{χ_x} should probably be q_x^{χ_x} or q^{deg(x)χ_x} for non-rational points x. This is not tracked here.

ideas.what: Global constant of the functional equation of L(X,E,t) expressed as a determinant of Frobenius on cohomology (δ^q(E_η)), with normalised version ε^q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (cohomological interpretation of L-functions, ~1964); presented in Deligne's papers
ideas.where_published: SGA 5 (Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L); Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 279 (1964)

ideas.what: Square of the global constant equals the product of squared local constants, derived via duality and a local computation of δ(μ_x)
ideas.modern_name: Product formula for ε-factors up to sign (ε^2 version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Deligne (1973, Antwerp II, 'Les constantes des équations fonctionnelles des fonctions L'); full formula proved by Laumon (1987, Publ. IHÉS 65). Partial and up-to-root-of-unity results by Deligne.

ideas.what: Local constants δ_x, ε_x attached to the local Galois representation α_x(E_η), normalised by q^{χ_x/2}
ideas.modern_name: Local ε-factors ε(V_x, ψ_x) of Langlands–Deligne

missed.claim: Grothendieck had, in manuscript, a derivation of the geometric product formula for ε-constants up to sign. The derivation squares the constant and uses duality together with a local computation δ(μ_x) = δ_x^{-2} q^{χ_x}. He leaves the sign undetermined. This predates Deligne's 1973 conjecture (if the dating 1962–71 holds) and Laumon's 1987 proof.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck already aimed at the local-to-global decomposition of ε-constants in the geometric case. Specialists generally attribute that programme to Langlands and Deligne. The squaring-via-duality argument itself is not new mathematically, since the sign is the hard part.

deep.surprise_reason: An unpublished up-to-sign version of the product formula for ε-factors in Grothendieck's hand is a notable historical detail. The mathematics, however, stops at the easy (squared) part, and the full result is well established (Deligne–Laumon).
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the exponent reads p^{-χ^q(E)(p+1)} in the image (the transcription has this). It is probably intended as q^{-χ(E)(q+1)} or similar. The scribbled line after 'D(E_η^q),' likely reads 'on lit' or 'on tire'.
In the bracket of the second display the image shows p^{-χ_x(E_η)(q+1)}. The transcription is consistent with the image, but the mix of p and q is in the original.
The line beginning 'δ^q(E_η)^2/q^{χ^q(E)}' contains a crossed-out fragment '= q^{χ^q(E)}'. This is correctly marked as deleted.
The last equality on the ε line reads (∏ δ_x(E_η)/p^{χ_x(E_η)/2})·1/p^{χ/2} in the image, with a crossed-out mark before χ_x.
